newsitem.title: USA: Ohio treasurer warns pensions on beating market.
newsitem.headline: Ohio treasurer warns pensions on beating market.

text.p: Ohio Treasurer J. Kenneth Blackwell said Wednesday that too many public pension funds are run to "beat the market" and not to ensure the funding of liabilities.

Blackwell, who spoke at the National Association of State Auditors, Comptrollers and Treasurers' National Public Pension Funds Conference in Cleveland, said pension fund managers were acting more like stock brokers or "bond market gurus," gauging their success against benchmarks like the S&P 500 stock index or the long bond.
"Beating the market in the short term means very little if you can't pay up in the long term," Blackwell said.
He added that the asset allocation of pension portfolios must match the term structure of their liabilities.

"Pension fund managers' number one objective must be to ensure the funding of liabilities," he said. "Asset allocation, contribution rates, budget projections, all these should be driven by consideration of your fund's liabilities, not the other way around."
